title: Claim History and Early Access to Reimbursements on Payout Methods
content:
A host's recent claim history limits how much of a same-day claim reimbursement a Payout Methods on-request payout advances. The on-request claim advance share, the part of the claim reimbursements credited to the method on the request date that the payout includes, is multiplied according to the reimbursements paid on the host's Host Damage Protection (HostCover) plans.

## Rule

The claim advance share is multiplied:

- by **0.60** when the host's HostCover plans record **3 or more** reimbursements paid less than 24 whole months before the request date, the one credited on the request date included;
- by **0.80** when they record **exactly 2**;
- by **one** otherwise.

## What is counted

- **Records:** the reimbursement-paid entries on the ledgers of all the host's HostCover plans, by the date each was paid.
- **Window:** reimbursements paid less than 24 whole months before the request date. A reimbursement paid exactly 24 whole months before the request date is outside the window.
- **Today's reimbursement:** a reimbursement credited on the request date is counted.

## Count-to-multiplier table

| Reimbursements paid in the window | Multiplier on the claim advance share |
|---|---|
| 0 | One |
| 1 | One |
| 2 | 0.80 |
| 3 | 0.60 |
| 4 or more | 0.60 |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- An imagined host has a claim advance share of 50 percent and three reimbursements paid in the window, one of them credited on the request date. The share is multiplied by 0.60, giving 30 percent.
- An imagined request date of 2027-03-10: a reimbursement paid on 2025-03-10 is 24 whole months earlier and is not counted; one paid on 2025-03-11 is 23 whole months earlier and is counted.
- An imagined host with exactly 2 reimbursements in the window and a claim advance share of 100 percent: the share becomes 80 percent.
